items.stem: Demand variability doubles while the target service level and lead time stay the same. What happens to required safety stock?

options.text: It increases, because safety stock scales with demand variability
options.rationale: Correct: higher demand standard deviation requires more safety stock for the same service level.

options.text: It falls, because variability reduces the need for buffer
options.rationale: Greater variability increases, not reduces, the buffer needed.

options.text: It stays the same, because only lead time matters
options.rationale: Both demand variability and lead time drive safety stock.
Zero safety stock would collapse the service level under variability.

items.explanation: Correct: higher demand standard deviation requires more safety stock for the same service level.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: You are segmenting a range with ABC and XYZ. Which TWO statements correctly describe the axes? (Select TWO.)

options.text: ABC ranks items by value or spend contribution
options.rationale: Correct: ABC is a value/Pareto classification.

options.text: XYZ classifies items by demand variability or predictability
options.rationale: Correct: XYZ captures how steady or erratic demand is.

options.text: ABC ranks items by demand variability
options.rationale: Variability is the XYZ axis, not ABC.

options.text: XYZ ranks items by unit price only
options.rationale: XYZ is about variability, not price.

items.explanation: Correct: ABC is a value/Pareto classification.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An item has very high inventory turns but also frequent stockouts. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Safety stock or reorder point is set too low for the demand variability
options.rationale: Correct: high turns with stockouts points to under-buffering, not healthy flow.
Overstock would show low turns, not stockouts.

options.text: Turns and stockouts are unrelated and need no action
options.rationale: The pattern is a clear signal to revisit the policy.
Recurring stockouts indicate the policy or forecast needs work.

items.explanation: Correct: high turns with stockouts points to under-buffering, not healthy flow.
